title: the WSG flying mounts
audit_label: R460 WSG flying mounts pin audit
audit_comment: The flying-mounts slice pins Table 27, the characteristics of flying mounts: the four category grids (A the 20 dragons and dragonlike, B the 6 birds, C the 7 winged mammals, D the 8 other fantastic creatures - 41 mounts x 7 columns: normal and maximum load with the dash as max = normal, the full and reduced move rates, the maneuverability class on the A=1..E=5 scale, and the safe-turns/rest stamina pair), the column definitions (the plummet rule over maximum, the single-rate 0 marker, the MC one-class drop when ridden with E unreducible, the over-load stamina cut of one turn or one-third whichever greater, inapplicable to the dash creatures), the solid-form footnote for the cloud and mist dragons, the listing criteria (Prime Material, wilderness, size M or L air-carrier), the trained-mount scarcity and the untrained at-mercy rule, the coerced-mount refusals, the triple-to-fifty rations feeding, and the saddle/container even-distribution encumbrance rules with the 2:1 doubling (rules/wsgflymounts.h, prefix wfm); census 384 -> 385.

banner.title: The WSG FLYING MOUNTS, R460: using a flying mount changes the way a character looks at things - terrain becomes scenery and long distance takes on a new meaning, but there is no place to hide from arrows, hailstones or lightning, and falling out of a saddle several hundred feet up is more than momentary discomfort. Table 27, the CHARACTERISTICS OF FLYING MOUNTS, in four categories: A, dragons and dragonlike creatures - black dragon 9000/18000 at 24/12 with stamina 24/6, blue and bronze 15000/30000 with 27/6, brass as the black, celestial 5000/10000 at 48/24 with 12/6, cloud dragon 18000/36000 at 39/18 with 30/6 (ridden only in solid form, as the mist dragon 18000/36000 at 33/15 with the same stamina), coiled 3000/4500 at 12/6, copper 12000/24000, dracolisk 3000/5000 at 15/6 with 2/1, dragonne 1500 at a single 9 rate with 2/1, dragonnel 6000/10000 at 18/9 MC D with 12/3, earth 2000/3000, gold 21000/42000 at 30/15 with 30/6, green 12000/18000, red and silver 18000/36000 with 30/6, spirit 4000/6500 at 12/6, white 6000/12000 at 30/15 with 18/6, and wyvern 10000/20000 at 24/12 with 18/6; B, birds and birdlike - boobrie 1000/1500 at 15/9 with the unusual 3/3 stamina, giant eagle 1000/1500 at 48/18 with 9/3, pteranodon 1500 at a single 15 rate MC D with 2/1, giant pterosaur 2000 at a single 12 rate with 3/1, roc 50000/100000 at 30/15 with 30/6, and giant vulture 1000/1500 at 24/12 with 3/2; C, winged mammals - chimera 4500 at a single 18 rate with 12/3, griffon 5500/8000 at 30/15 MC D with 18/6, gorgimera 5000 at a single 15 rate, hippogriff 4000/6000 at 36/18 MC D with 15/3, manticore 3000 at a single 18 rate with 6/3, opinicus 1000/1500 at 30/15 MC C with 3/1, and pegasus 4000/6500 at 48/24 MC D with 12/3; D, other fantastic - aarakocra 1500 at a single 36 rate MC D with 3/2, androsphinx 7500/9500 with 18/6, criosphinx 7000/9000 with 15/6, dragon horse 3000/5000 at 48/24 MC C with 12/3, gynosphinx 5000/8000 with 15/6, hieracosphinx 7000/8500 at 36/18 with 18/6, giant mantis 2000/3000 at 12/6 with 6/3, and yeth hound 2000/3000 at 27/12 MC C with 9/3. The columns: normal load is the encumbrance carried at the full rate; maximum load is the greatest load while aloft (a dash means normal is also maximum; anything more and the mount is unable or unwilling to leave the ground, or plummets to the nearest landing spot); the move rate is full/reduced in miles per half-day (a 0 right of the slash means one rate always); the MC when ridden is always one class lower than natural, except E which cannot be reduced; and the stamina is safe turns aloft / turns of rest, with the over-normal-load flying time cut by one turn or one-third of normal, whichever is greater (inapplicable to dash creatures, which cannot fly at all over their normal load). The listed mounts come from the Monster Manual, the Fiend Folio, and Monster Manual II: native to the Prime Material, normally found in a wilderness, and size M or L able to carry through the air; the DM assigns stats for unlisted creatures using the table as a guide. Trained mounts are not easy to find and not cheap; an untrained uncooperative beast can be ridden but the rider is at its mercy. A coerced mount may refuse loads, fly slowly, or insist on rest - full benefit requires willingness. Feeding: most need at least triple rations daily, up to fifty rations for one of the biggest dragon types, and the specialized appetites (the manticore preferring human flesh) may force hunting with the mount. Loads need saddle and containers, ideally distributed evenly on both sides; a load twice as heavy on one side doubles its entire encumbrance value.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed pp. 47-48; the user own copy OCR (pages 48-49) cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0047/0048) - the djvu GARBLES the Table 27 word layer (rows misaligned, labels and values dropped), so the grid was settled by TWO independent IIIF eye-reads of leaf $47 which agree with the OCR exactly on all 41 rows and all 7 columns - with the cloud dragon move rate resolved at high resolution (native 2411px crop) as 39/18, the bulk 1600px reads misresolving the 9 as a 3, as both text layers read 39.

consts.name: wfmCatACount
consts.comment: Category A, the dragons and dragonlike creatures: black, blue, brass, bronze, celestial, cloud, coiled, copper, dracolisk, dragonne, dragonnel, earth, gold, green, mist, red, silver, spirit, white and wyvern.

consts.name: wfmCatBCount
consts.comment: Category B, the birds and birdlike creatures: boobrie, giant eagle, pteranodon, giant pterosaur, roc and giant vulture.

consts.name: wfmCatCCount
consts.comment: Category C, the winged mammalian creatures: chimera, griffon, gorgimera, hippogriff, manticore, opinicus and pegasus.

consts.name: wfmCatDCount
consts.comment: Category D, the other fantastic creatures: aarakocra, androsphinx, criosphinx, dragon horse, gynosphinx, hieracosphinx, giant mantis and yeth hound.

consts.name: wfmTotalCreatures
consts.comment: The four categories total 41 flying mounts, drawn from the Monster Manual, the Fiend Folio and Monster Manual II.

consts.name: wfmMcRiddenDrop
consts.comment: The MC when carrying a rider or equipment is always one class lower than the natural class.

consts.name: wfmMcFloor
consts.comment: A natural maneuverability class of E (5 on the A=1..E=5 scale) cannot be reduced any further.

consts.name: wfmOverloadStaCutTurns
consts.comment: Carrying more than a normal load cuts the safe flying time by one turn...

consts.name: wfmOverloadStaThird
consts.comment: ...or by one-third of the normal stamina rating, whichever is greater.

consts.name: wfmRationsMultiple
consts.comment: Most flying mounts need at least triple rations of food and water each day compared to a human.

consts.name: wfmBigDragonRations
consts.comment: One of the biggest dragon types may need as much as fifty rations per day.

bools.name: wfmTrainedScarceAndDear
bools.comment: Creatures trained for use as mounts may not be easy to locate, and they will not come cheap.

bools.name: wfmUntrainedAtMercy
bools.comment: An untrained uncooperative creature can still be ridden, but without magical assistance the rider is completely at the mercy of the beast, which goes where it wants and will not voluntarily keep the rider aboard.

bools.name: wfmOverMaxNeverLifts
bools.comment: A mount asked to carry more than its maximum load will be unable or unwilling to leave the ground.

bools.name: wfmOverMaxPlummets
bools.comment: A mount already aloft when overloaded will immediately plummet toward the nearest landing spot.

bools.name: wfmDashMaxEqualsNormal
bools.comment: A printed dash for maximum load means the normal load is also the maximum load.

bools.name: wfmDashCannotFlyOverNormal
bools.comment: A creature with no maximum-load rating cannot fly at all if its normal load amount is exceeded.

bools.name: wfmReducedRateWhenOverloaded
bools.comment: The right-of-slash reduced move rate goes into effect whenever the mount is burdened above a normal load.

bools.name: wfmZeroRateMeansSingleRate
bools.comment: A 0 right of the slash means the creature has only one movement rate, which always applies as long as it is able and willing to fly.

bools.name: wfmMcDropsWhenRidden
bools.comment: The MC when ridden is one class lower than natural (B to C, C to D, and so on).

bools.name: wfmMcEStaysE
bools.comment: Beasts with a natural MC of E keep class E when ridden - it cannot be reduced any further.

bools.name: wfmStaCutIsGreaterOf
bools.comment: The over-normal-load safe-time cut is the greater of one turn and one-third of the normal stamina rating.

bools.name: wfmStaRestBetweenFlights
bools.comment: The right stamina figure is the turns of rest needed between flights to retain full strength and carrying capacity.

bools.name: wfmCloudMistSolidFormOnly
bools.comment: The cloud dragon and the mist dragon can only be ridden when in solid form.

bools.name: wfmListedIfPrimeMaterial
bools.comment: Listing criterion: the creature is native to, or normally found on, the Prime Material Plane.

bools.name: wfmListedIfWildernessNative
bools.comment: Listing criterion: the creature is normally found in a wilderness, not a subterranean, environment.

bools.name: wfmListedIfSizeMOrL
bools.comment: Listing criterion: the creature is size M or L with a physical form able to carry passengers or objects through the air.

bools.name: wfmDmAssignsUnlistedStats
bools.comment: For an unlisted creature serving as aerial transport, the DM assigns statistics using its game description and the table as guidelines.

bools.name: wfmCoercedMaySkimp
bools.comment: A beast forced to serve against its will may refuse to carry more than its coercer, may fly more slowly, or may insist on more frequent rest.

bools.name: wfmFullBenefitNeedsWillingness
bools.comment: Full benefit in carrying capacity, movement, maneuverability and stamina requires a willing mount, even if the willingness is temporary and artificially induced.

bools.name: wfmLoadsNeedContainers
bools.comment: A flying mount will rarely carry equipment or cargo that is not contained - a bare treasure chest brings at least a movement reduction.

bools.name: wfmUnevenLoadRaisesEnc
bools.comment: The encumbrance value of the load rises with the side imbalance: doubled when one side carries twice the other, and so forth.
